_doc: Inflation benchmarks for retrospective editions dated in 2022: the target for the current calendar year as publicly known at each cutoff. End-2021 state of the verified 2021 register (its four 2021 changes — New Zealand's replacement remit of 25 Feb 2021, China's ~3% objective of 5 Mar 2021, India's re-notified 4% ±2 target of 31 Mar 2021, the ECB's symmetric 2% target of 8 Jul 2021 — are the starting rows, and the general note is the one restated from 8 Jul 2021), updated for the 2022 current-year targets set earlier: Brazil 3.75 → 3.50% ±1.5 (CMN Res. 4,724 of 27 Jun 2019, art. 1; DOU 1 Jul 2019); Indonesia 3% ±1 (PMK 101/PMK.010/2021, set 28 Jul and promulgated 29 Jul 2021, Art. 2(3)(a)); Thailand 2.0, the midpoint of the 1–3% headline range approved by the Cabinet on 14 Dec 2021 (The Bangkok Insight and Thansettakij the same day, Bangkok Post 15 Dec; the BoT announcement No. 2/2564, dated 16 Dec 2021, is a scanned PDF read from the page images and, like its unofficial English translation, is cited only from the file's creation on 23 Dec 2021); Türkiye 5% ±2pp, the 'medium-term' target maintained (CBRT Monetary and Exchange Rate Policy for 2022, 29 Dec 2021, paras 13–14; the Turkish and English PDFs were both created that day); Colombia 3% with a 2–4% range (Board of 26 Nov 2021; banrep.gov.co sits behind a bot check, so the decision is cited from Portafolio, Valora Analitik and La FM of the same day); Canada's wording replaced by the Joint Statement on the Renewal of the Monetary Policy Framework of 13 Dec 2021 (the 2% midpoint of the 1–3% range kept for another five years; value unchanged). Korea's 2% (no fixed period) and India's 4% are carried. One change announced during 2022: China's Report on the Work of the Government delivered 5 Mar 2022 (CPI 'around 3%', value unchanged; recorded as the new year's objective; applies from 2022-03-13). Value-unchanged reaffirmations are not recorded: the FOMC's reaffirmation effective 25 Jan 2022; the UK remit of 17 Nov 2022 ('re-confirm the inflation target as 2 per cent'); the SNB's 2022 strategy review (definition of price stability unchanged); India's MPC resolutions; the Colombian Board of 25 Nov 2022 reiterating 3%. Targets set during 2022 for later years are not recorded (Brazil's 2025 target, CMN Res. 5,018 of 23 Jun 2022), nor are announcements after the last edition's cutoff of 17 Dec 2022 (the BoK's Review on Inflation Targeting Operations of 20 Dec 2022; Thailand's Cabinet approval of 27 Dec 2022; the CBRT's Monetary Policy and Liraization Strategy for 2023 of 30 Dec 2022). New Zealand's 2021 remit stayed in force throughout 2022 (the first five-yearly remit review began that year), and no new Statement on the Conduct of Monetary Policy was issued in Australia during 2022. The ECB, BoJ, Riksbank, Norges Bank, MNB, CNB, NBP, Banxico, SARB and Banco Central de Chile targets are unchanged (checked against 2022 publications); Switzerland is carried without a 2022-dated primary check (no change is known; the SNB's 2022 strategy review kept the definition). Every new source was fetched and its quoted text checked; sources are shown only once published; no wording names a later year.
note: Where an official objective refers to an index other than headline CPI (the Federal Reserve's PCE price index; see each row), the benchmark is applied to headline CPI. India's benchmark is the RBI's stated CPI objective for the current period. Benchmarks apply to the headline CPI series used here. Each benchmark is the target for the current calendar year as publicly known at the cutoff; China's is the government's annual CPI objective from its Report on the Work of the Government (until that report, the previous year's applies). Where a range was set, its midpoint is used; for the euro area, the ECB's symmetric 2% target. Sources are listed only if published on or before the edition’s last eligible day.

US.wording: FOMC Statement on Longer-Run Goals and Monetary Policy Strategy as amended 27 Aug 2020: the longer-run goal of 2 percent PCE inflation is kept, and the Committee 'seeks to achieve inflation that averages 2 percent over time', so that 'following periods when inflation has been running persistently below 2 percent, appropriate monetary policy will likely aim to achieve inflation moderately above 2 percent for some time' (value unchanged).
US.index: PCE price index; benchmark applied to headline CPI

urls.label: Federal Reserve press release, 'Federal Open Market Committee announces approval of updates to its Statement on Longer-Run Goals and Monetary Policy Strategy', 27 Aug 2020

XM.wording: ECB strategy review, 8 Jul 2021: 'The Governing Council considers that price stability is best maintained by aiming for a 2% inflation target over the medium term. This target is symmetric, meaning negative and positive deviations of inflation from the target are equally undesirable' (replacing 'below, but close to, 2%'; HICP remains the measure).

urls.label: ECB press release, 'ECB's Governing Council approves its new monetary policy strategy', 8 Jul 2021

JP.wording: 'The "Price Stability Target" under the Framework for the Conduct of Monetary Policy', 22 Jan 2013: 'the Bank sets the "price stability target" at 2 percent in terms of the year-on-year rate of change in the consumer price index (CPI)' (replacing the 1% 'price stability goal' of February 2012); in the joint statement with the Government the Bank will 'aim to achieve this target at the earliest possible time'.

urls.label: Bank of Japan, The "Price Stability Target" under the Framework for the Conduct of Monetary Policy, 22 Jan 2013
Joint Statement of the Government and the Bank of Japan on Overcoming Deflation and Achieving Sustainable Economic Growth, 22 Jan 2013

GB.wording: June Budget 2010: 'the independent Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) of the Bank of England will continue to target 2 per cent inflation, as measured by the 12-month increase in the Consumer Prices Index (CPI)'.

urls.label: HM Treasury, Budget 2010 (June, HC 61), 22 Jun 2010, para 1.27

CA.wording: Joint Statement of the Government of Canada and the Bank of Canada on the Renewal of the Monetary Policy Framework, 13 Dec 2021: 'The target will continue to be defined in terms of the 12-month rate of change in the total CPI. The inflation target will continue to be the 2 percent mid-point of the 1 to 3 percent inflation-control range'; the agreement runs for another five-year period, beginning with 2022. 'The primary objective of monetary policy is to maintain low, stable inflation over time'; monetary policy 'should continue to support maximum sustainable employment', and the Bank 'will continue to use the flexibility of the 1 to 3 percent control range to actively seek the maximum sustainable level of employment when conditions warrant' (value unchanged).

urls.label: Bank of Canada, Joint Statement of the Government of Canada and the Bank of Canada on the Renewal of the Monetary Policy Framework, 13 Dec 2021

AU.wording: Statement on the Conduct of Monetary Policy, 19 Sep 2016: 'They agree that an appropriate goal is to keep consumer price inflation between 2 and 3 per cent, on average, over time' (midpoint 2.5%; the previous Statement said 'over the cycle').

urls.label: RBA Statement on the Conduct of Monetary Policy, 19 Sep 2016

CH.wording: The SNB 'regards prices as stable when the national consumer price index (CPI) rises by less than 2% per annum' (midpoint of 0–2%: 1.0%).

urls.label: SNB Quarterly Bulletin 4/2007, 'Inflation forecasting as part of the monetary policy concept'

SE.wording: Riksbank, 7 Sep 2017: 'The Executive Board of the Riksbank has decided to adopt inflation measured in terms of the CPIF (the consumer price index with a fixed interest rate) as a formal target variable for monetary policy. The target for monetary policy is that the annual change in the CPIF shall be 2 per cent, that is, the same level previously applied to the CPI'; a variation band of 1–3 per cent replaces the ±1pp tolerance band, applying from the monetary policy decision of 6 Sep 2017.
SE.index: CPIF (CPI with a fixed interest rate); benchmark applied to headline CPI

urls.label: Sveriges Riksbank press release No. 21, 'CPIF target variable for monetary policy', 7 Sep 2017

NO.wording: Regulation on Monetary Policy laid down by the Government on 2 Mar 2018 (in force immediately; the 2001 regulation repealed from the same date), Section 3: 'The operational target of monetary policy shall be annual consumer price inflation of close to 2 percent over time. Inflation targeting shall be forward-looking and flexible so that it can contribute to high and stable output and employment and to counteracting the build-up of financial imbalances.' Norges Bank: 'The inflation target is now 2%, compared with the previous 2.5%.'

urls.label: Norges Bank Monetary Policy Report 1/18, 15 Mar 2018 (reproduces the Regulation of 2 March 2018 on Monetary Policy, p. 13)
Norges Bank, Executive Board's assessment, Monetary Policy Report 1/18, 15 Mar 2018

NZ.wording: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Replacement of Remit for Monetary Policy Committee) Order 2021 (LI 2021/29, made 22 Feb 2021, notified 25 Feb 2021): the inflation objective is unchanged — 'keep future annual inflation between 1 and 3 percent over the medium term, with a focus on keeping future inflation near the 2 percent mid-point' — and the Committee shall, in pursuing its operational objectives, 'assess the effect of its monetary policy decisions on the Government's policy [to support more sustainable house prices]' (value unchanged; recorded because the remit is replaced).

urls.label: New Zealand Gazette, notice 2021-dl640: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Replacement of Remit for Monetary Policy Committee) Order 2021, LI 2021/29, 25 Feb 2021
Westpac Economic Bulletin, housing remit update (quoting the new remit clause), 25 Feb 2021

CN.wording: Report on the Work of the Government delivered 5 Mar 2021, main projected targets for this year: 'CPI increase of around 3 percent' ('居民消费价格涨幅3%左右'; a government objective, not a PBoC target; the previous year's was around 3.5%).

IN.wording: On 31 Mar 2021 the Government retained the CPI inflation target at 4 per cent with lower and upper tolerance levels of 2 and 6 per cent for the next five years, from April 2021 (value unchanged; recorded because the statutory target was re-notified); the MPC's resolutions keep setting policy 'in consonance with the objective of achieving the medium-term target for consumer price index (CPI) inflation of 4 per cent within a band of +/- 2 per cent'.

urls.label: ETV Bharat (PTI), the Government asks the RBI to keep retail inflation at 4 per cent with a 2 per cent margin for another five years, 31 Mar 2021
RBI, Governor's Statement, 7 Apr 2021 (para 11: 'On March 31, 2021, the Government retained the inflation target at 4 per cent')

BR.wording: CMN Resolution 4,724 of 27 Jun 2019, art. 1: 'É fixada, para o ano de 2022, a meta para a inflação de 3,50% (três inteiros e cinquenta centésimos por cento), com intervalo de tolerância de menos 1,50 p.p. (um e meio ponto percentual) e de mais 1,50 p.p. (um e meio ponto percentual)' (3.50% with a ±1.5pp tolerance band).

urls.label: CMN Resolution 4,724 of 27 Jun 2019, art. 1 (2022 target; published in the DOU of 1 Jul 2019)

MX.wording: 'Annual CPI inflation of 3 percent' with a variability interval of ±1 percentage point.

ZA.wording: Budget Speech, 17 Feb 2010: 'I wish to confirm that the Reserve Bank will continue to pursue a target for CPI inflation of 3 to 6 per cent' (midpoint 4.5%).

urls.label: Minister of Finance, Budget Speech 2010, 17 Feb 2010

TR.wording: Medium-term CPI inflation target of 5%, set jointly with the Government: the CBRT's Monetary and Exchange Rate Policy for 2022 (29 Dec 2021), para 13: 'Hükümetle birlikte belirlenen orta vadeli enflasyon hedefi yüzde 5 olarak korunmuştur' ('The medium-term inflation target of 5% set jointly with the Government has been maintained'); 'While converging to the medium-term inflation target, the targets announced by the CBRT via Inflation Reports will serve as interim targets and a reference to inflation expectations.' Para 14: the uncertainty band 'has been maintained at 2 percentage points in both directions around the inflation target, the same as the previous years.' The agreed 5% target is used; the Inflation Report interim targets are not.

ID.wording: Inflation target for 2022 of 3% with a deviation of 1%, fixed by Finance Minister Regulation 101/PMK.010/2021 (set 28 Jul 2021, promulgated 29 Jul 2021), Article 2(3)(a): '3,0% (tiga persen) untuk tahun 2022' … 'dengan deviasi sebesar 1,0% (satu persen)' (annual CPI inflation, year-on-year, at year-end: 'Inflasi IHK tahunan (year-on-year) di akhir tahun', Article 2(1); a point with deviation, 'titik dengan toleransi (point with deviation)', Article 2(2)).

KR.wording: Price stability target from 2019 set by the Monetary Policy Board on 26 Dec 2018, in consultation with the Government: 2% in terms of the year-on-year rate of change in the consumer price index ('2019년 이후 물가안정목표'를 소비자물가 상승률(전년 동기 대비) 기준 2.0%로 확정 의결), the same level as the 2016–2018 target; the three-year application period is abolished (no fixed period), with the operation of the target reviewed every two years ('3년마다 재설정했던 물가안정목표의 적용기간을 없앴다. 다만, 2년 주기로 물가안정목표 운영 개선에 필요한 사항을 점검키로 했다').

urls.label: NewDaily Economy, Bank of Korea keeps its price stability target at 2.0% (in Korean), 26 Dec 2018
YTN, Bank of Korea monetary policy direction and price stability target (in Korean), 26 Dec 2018

CL.wording: Updated framework document 'La Política Monetaria del Banco Central de Chile en el Marco de Metas de Inflación' (published 11 Feb 2020): 'El nivel de meta para la inflación está fijado en 3% anual. Ello significa que la política monetaria se orienta a que la variación anual del IPC fluctúe en torno a 3%' and 'El propósito práctico u objetivo operacional de la política monetaria es que la inflación proyectada se ubique en 3% anual en un horizonte de política en torno a dos años' (value unchanged; the ±1pp range no longer defines the target: inflation 'debería fluctuar la mayor parte del tiempo en un rango de entre 2 y 4%').

urls.label: Diario Financiero, 'Banco Central actualiza marco de la política monetaria' (in Spanish), 12 Feb 2020

CO.wording: Board of Directors, 26 Nov 2021: the Board kept the inflation target for the year at 3%, with the range kept between 2% and 4% ('mantuvo en 3 % la meta de inflación de Colombia de cara al 2022. Así mismo, el rango para la inflación de Colombia en 2022 se mantiene entre 2 % y 4 %', Valora Analitik; the Board 'fijó este viernes, 26 de noviembre, una meta de inflación de 3% en un rango entre 2% y 4% para el próximo año', La FM). The Banco de la República's own page sits behind a bot check and could not be read; the decision is cited from same-day reports.

TH.wording: Monetary-policy target for 2022 approved by the Cabinet on 14 Dec 2021, as agreed between the Minister of Finance and the Monetary Policy Committee: headline inflation within the range of 1–3 percent as the medium-term price-stability target and the target for 2022 ('รัฐมนตรีว่าการกระทรวงการคลังและ กนง. มีข้อตกลงร่วมกันโดยกำหนดให้อัตราเงินเฟ้อทั่วไปในช่วงร้อยละ 1-3 เป็นเป้าหมายนโยบายการเงินด้านเสถียรภาพราคาสำหรับระยะปานกลาง และเป็นเป้าหมายสำหรับปี 2565'; BoT unofficial translation: 'the headline inflation was to reside within the range of 1.0 – 3.0 percent for the medium-term horizon and for the year 2022'); a range with no point target, the same as for 2021 (midpoint 2.0% used).
